itrpv-2026.title: International Technology Roadmap for Photovoltaic (ITRPV), 17th edition
itrpv-2026.note: The roadmap PDF is distributed by VDMA; the 2025 shares we quote were presented by ITRPV steering committee chair Markus Fischer and reported by TaiyangNews (taiyangnews-itrpv-2026) and PV Tech (pv-tech-itrpv-2026).

taiyangnews-itrpv-2026.title: ITRPV expects TOPCon to lead as BC and tandem technologies expand
taiyangnews-itrpv-2026.note: Report of the ITRPV 17th edition talk: in 2025 TOPCon about 75 % of crystalline-silicon cell production, PERC about 14 %, HJT about 5 %, TOPCon-based back contact about 5 %, HJT-based back contact about 0.1 %.

pv-tech-itrpv-2026.title: ITRPV 2026: solar industry maintains historic learning curve despite market turbulence
pv-tech-itrpv-2026.note: ITRPV 17th edition: mass-production module efficiency in 2025 of 21.7 % (p-type PERC), 23.5 % (TOPCon and HJT), 24.1 % (TOPCon back contact); n-type wafers about 82 %; c-Si about 98 % and thin film about 2 %.

paudyal-imenes-2021.note: Datasheet coefficients of the modules studied (Table 2), power then open-circuit voltage: mono c-Si −0.38 and −0.28 %/°C, multi c-Si −0.41 and −0.31 %/°C, heterojunction (Panasonic HIT) −0.29 and −0.25 %/°C, CIGS (Solibro) −0.38 and −0.29 %/°C.

first-solar-series-7.title: Series 7 FT1 module datasheet
first-solar-series-7.note: CdTe thin-film module: 505–550 W, efficiency 18.1–19.7 %, power temperature coefficient −0.32 %/°C, Voc coefficient −0.28 %/°C, warranted degradation 0.3 % per year.

jinko-tiger-neo.title: Tiger Neo (N-type TOPCon modules) product page
jinko-tiger-neo.note: Manufacturer figures: power temperature coefficient −0.29 %/°C versus −0.35 %/°C for p-type cells; first-year degradation at most 1 %, then 0.4 % per year.

pveducation-czochralski.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-czochralski.title: Czochralski silicon (PVEducation)
pveducation-czochralski.note: Cz ingots grow from quartz crucibles, which add about 1e18 cm⁻³ oxygen; boron-oxygen degradation in p-type, none in phosphorus-doped n-type.

pveducation-multicrystalline.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-multicrystalline.title: Multi-crystalline silicon (PVEducation)
pveducation-multicrystalline.note: Cast as a slab, cut into bricks, sliced; grain boundaries add recombination and shunts. Mono became dominant from 2018, helped by PERC, which benefits mono more.

pveducation-refining.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-refining.title: Refining silicon (PVEducation)
pveducation-refining.note: Quartz reduced with carbon in an arc furnace to metallurgical-grade silicon (about 98 %); Siemens process via trichlorosilane, distilled, then deposited on hot rods at about 1100 °C.

pveducation-arc.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-arc.title: Anti-reflection coatings (PVEducation)
pveducation-arc.note: Bare silicon reflects over 30 %; quarter-wave thickness d = λ0/(4·n1); ideal index n1 = √(n0·n2); silicon taken as n = 3.5.

pveducation-bypass.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-bypass.title: Bypass diodes (PVEducation)
pveducation-bypass.note: A bypass diode across a group of cells limits the reverse bias on a shaded cell and prevents hot spots; about 15 silicon cells per diode at most for full protection; a 36-cell module typically has 2.

pveducation-noct.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-noct.title: Nominal operating cell temperature (PVEducation)
pveducation-noct.note: NOCT: open-circuit cell temperature at 800 W/m², 20 °C air, 1 m/s wind, open back; most modules 40–45 °C.

pveducation-temperature.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-temperature.title: Effect of temperature (PVEducation)
pveducation-temperature.note: Silicon: Voc falls about 2.2 mV/°C; Isc rises about 0.06 %/°C; I0 follows B'·T^γ·exp(−Eg0/kT) with Eg0 ≈ 1.2 eV and γ ≈ 3.

pveducation-voc.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-voc.title: Open-circuit voltage (PVEducation)
pveducation-voc.note: Voc depends on the light-generated and saturation currents (current densities), not on cell size; commercial silicon cells typically about 690 mV, best laboratory cells up to 764 mV at one sun.
